resources.string: Take a photo or pick one from your library, adjust it, then read it with OvisOCR2.
1. Choose an image\n2. Crop, rotate, and clean it up\n3. Read, edit, and save the text
The full photo stays in app storage, so you can change the region later.
Only the selected region is stored; the rest of the photo, including a camera capture, is deleted.
Region %1$d × %2$d px · drag corners or edges
Image preview. Drag the corners or edges of the frame to select the region to read.
Adjust the region, rotation, and colours, then tap Run OCR.
OCR text appears here. Edit it as plain text, or select words to highlight their image region.
Document image with highlights for selected OCR text
Select text to highlight its image region. Edited or unmatched words have no reliable region.
No reliable image region for this selection. It may be edited, unmatched, or outside the localizer\'s supported script.
Choose a photo or use the camera.
Engine: OvisOCR2 %1$s on this device. Images stay on the phone.
Engine: OvisOCR2 %1$s on this device, but the model folder is not imported. Open Settings from the menu.
Engine: cloud %1$s at %2$s.\nImages are uploaded to this server for OCR.
Engine: cloud, but the server URL or model is not saved. Open Model settings.
Reading with OvisOCR2 %1$s on this device. Keep this screen open; CPU inference can take a few minutes.
Sending the image to cloud model %1$s and waiting for the result…
OCR complete. Locating text regions on the device…
Cancellation requested. Waiting for the current operation to stop.
OCR complete: %1$.1f s. Tokens: %2$d. Aligned words: %3$d. Verify important content.
Output reached the %1$d-token limit and is incomplete. Use a smaller crop.
OCR text is available, but highlighting failed: %1$s
On-device inference is experimental and CPU-only. Physical ARM64 phone performance is not yet verified. More than 6 GB RAM is recommended.
This device has 6 GB RAM or less. On-device inference may fail; use Q4 or a cloud server.
Choose where OCR runs. Changes apply to the next OCR run.
On-device engines never send images off the phone. The cloud engine uploads each image to the server you configure.
Download ovisocr2-q4.zip (or ovisocr2-bf16.zip) from the OCRDroid GitHub release, extract it, then import the extracted folder. Weights are verified and copied into private app storage.
BF16 uses substantially more RAM and storage. Select an exported BF16 GGUF folder, not raw safetensors.
Import a model folder for this precision first.
Copying and checking model weights. This needs additional device storage.
Use a server that exposes the OpenAI chat completions API, for example: vllm serve ATH-MaaS/OvisOCR2 (vLLM 0.22.1 or newer). A URL without a path uses /v1.
Sent as a Bearer token; stored encrypted
This URL uses http://, so images, OCR text, and the API key are sent unencrypted. Use https:// unless the server is on a network you trust.
Connected, but model %1$s is not served. Served models: %2$s
Highlights use bundled ML Kit text localization on the device, not OvisOCR2 boxes, for both local and cloud OCR. Matching is best-effort; no guessed boxes are drawn.
